rule: docs/slices/locale-1.md § 16.2 item 5 (coverage rule), for NEWSLETTER-1 (docs/slices/newsletter-1.md): the six site keys of the newsletter form (`newsletterTexts`, packages/shared/src/locale-strings.ts). They reach a page only in the `_newsletter` of a newsletter block (renderer prepareBlocks) or in the public popups answer of a newsletter popup that collects addresses; the reader is `NewsletterForm` (packages/plugins/src/newsletter). Their checks render the real block (server HTML in German and French, the browser states in Romanian) and the serving row asserts the en-US form on the running build; the consent line is also the text the backend stores (backend/test/unit/newsletter-1.test.ts). None is a count key. Checked by renderer/test/unit/locale-coverage.test.ts.

site.newsletterEmail.case: German tenant: the German consent line beside a required box, the email field, the German button
submits { email, source: \"newsletter\", consentText: the line drawn, consentLocale: its locale, recaptchaToken: null } to /api/leads

site.newsletterEmailPlaceholder.case: submits { email, source: \"newsletter\", consentText: the line drawn, consentLocale: its locale, recaptchaToken: null } to /api/leads

site.newsletterConsent.case: German tenant: the German consent line beside a required box, the email field, the German button
opted in with the answer's texts: the form in place of the link
the subscription holds an id, the time, the presentation locale and the exact line of its locale table (German pack for de-DE)

site.newsletterSubscribe.case: the owner's button label wins over the locale text; a blank one does not

site.newsletterSubscribing.case: while the answer is pending the button shows the locale \"subscribing\" text and is disabled
